purpose: Fixed report fields for independent simulated participant; outcomes limited to visible UI evidence.
persona: Independent simulated beginner, first introduction to RILL, interested in a short melodic instrumental.

rating_reasons.easy_to_use: Visible hints, Pencil, Mixer labels, and an on-screen naming keyboard allowed the entire requested workflow with a mouse. Exact trimming and the initial Duplicate tool behavior required adjustment.
rating_reasons.how_cool_it_looks: Restrained dark theme, distinct track colors, waveform and note previews, and visible routing lines looked organized and appealing.
rating_reasons.how_fast_it_is: Most edits gave immediate visible feedback and repeats were quick to build. WAV export showed an elapsed status; playback needed one recovery. This is an interaction impression under laboratory conditions, not a benchmark.
rating_reasons.how_confusing_it_is: The Duplicate button became a tool before copying, and initially dark meters followed by an audio stream error were confusing. Clear hints and Retry playback resolved these obstacles.
rating_reasons.feature_completeness: The observed UI covered audio, MIDI, the assigned VST3 instrument, mixing, buses, sends, naming, saving, and both exports. I did not evaluate broader production features or other plug-ins.

findings.observation: Double-clicking the visible MIDI creation area opened the Device library; assigning Rill Lab Sine created a MIDI track and editable pattern.
Drawing notes beyond the initial clip extended it to 8.705 seconds, slightly longer than the 8.571-second audio. Trimming the MIDI edge corrected the mismatch.
Duplicate selected a tool rather than copying immediately. The visible Click a clip to duplicate hint led to successful adjacent repeats; edge trims then produced a displayed duration of 0:30.000.
Mixer drags visibly changed audio and MIDI faders to -8.4 and -7.3 dB and pans to L15 and R17. Mute and Solo visibly highlighted when clicked.
Add bus created New bus. MIDI Add send > + Send > New bus created a visible 0.25x Post send; the Mixer showed Bus 1 in and Send · New bus.
The project Rename command exposed an on-screen keyboard. Mouse clicks named the project Moon drift, and Save supplied the matching filename in the native dialog.

WAV export displayed a 30-second arrangement and optional effect tails. After exporting without tails and exporting MIDI, Recent exports listed both under Completed exports; the MIDI Exported banner was also seen.
A Play attempt after export showed Audio output stream failed or disconnected. Earlier playback screenshots had advancing position but dark meters.
Retry playback returned the UI to Pause; subsequent screenshots showed an advancing playhead and lit audio, MIDI, bus, and master meters.

outcome.status: Completed through the visible UI: a named 30-second arrangement with audio and MIDI/VST, adjusted Mixer settings, bus/send, saved project, and both files listed as completed exports. Exported file contents remain independently unverified.
outcome.composition: Startup Circuit rhythm audio repeated across 14 bars at 112 BPM; a manually drawn 16-note melodic MIDI phrase repeated alongside it, with the final audio and MIDI repeats trimmed to 30 seconds. One bus receives a post-fader MIDI-track send.
outcome.playback_observed: Initial playback position advanced with dark meters. A later attempt showed an audio output stream failure/disconnection banner. Retry playback recovered visible playhead movement and lit audio/MIDI/bus/master meters; screenshots reached 003.04.19 and 008.01.53. Playback stopped at completion. No heard audio claim.

limitations: No exported file contents or heard audio claim; independent coordinator verification follows.
Artifact paths come from visible native save/export dialogs and their filenames, without filesystem inspection.
WAV completion was observed in the Completed exports list; its transient success banner was not captured before the MIDI status replaced it.
Mixer balance was set using displayed values, not by listening. Mute/solo button state was observed, not their audible effect.
Laboratory software graphics and timer-paced virtual audio sink with 60 ms buffering and a 1024-frame request at 48 kHz do not establish real hardware latency or audible quality.
Only the installed Rill Lab Sine VST3 was used. Elapsed session time includes tool, screenshot, and reporting overhead.

mixer_outcome.volume: Dragged audio fader from -6.0 to -8.4 dB and MIDI fader from -2.5 to -7.3 dB; both values remained visible in the final arrangement. No listening-based balance claim.
mixer_outcome.pan: Horizontal knob drags changed audio from C to L15 and MIDI from C to R17; final arrangement retained those values.
mixer_outcome.mute: Clicked audio Mute on and off twice; orange highlighting appeared when on. Restored off before final save. Audible behavior not auditioned.
mixer_outcome.solo: Clicked MIDI Solo on and off twice; highlighting appeared when on. Restored off before final save. Audible behavior not auditioned.
mixer_outcome.bus: Clicked Mixer Add bus, which created New bus at 0.0 dB routed to Master; after adding the send it displayed Bus 1 in. Bus meter later lit during recovered playback.
mixer_outcome.send: Clicked MIDI-track Add send, + Send, then New bus. Routing showed New bus at 0.25x with Post selected, and the Mixer displayed Send · New bus.
